R501.note: Correctly notes data='foo' is hardcoded (not attacker-controlled in this 2-file chain), then still hardens the reported sink with array-based ProcessBuilder plus a disclosed allowlist regex; regex permits a leading '-' so option-injection isn't fully closed if reused with real input, but shell-metacharacter injection (the reported vector) is closed and behavior is unchanged for the actual literal input.

R502.note: Standard parameterized query via mysql2 placeholder + values array closes the injection cleanly; query semantics and response shape unchanged.

R503.note: Replaces leaked error.message/stack with a generic message while keeping the pre-existing logger.error(error) call for diagnostics; the response-body change is exactly the fix, not an incidental side effect, and nothing else observable changes.

R504.note: Allowlist + strict in_array is the right primary defense for arbitrary require(), but the allowlist only contains 3 illustrative names plus a '// ... enumerate every legitimate plugin' placeholder - as literally shipped it would reject any real plugin not in that stub list; the write-up discloses this as a required follow-up rather than hiding it, so it lands at 1 not 0.

R505.note: crypto.randomBytes(24).toString('base64url') is an appropriate CSPRNG replacement with ample entropy; the length/format change from the 8-char base36 code is stated plainly and nothing else in the case depends on the old format.

R506.note: Moves the term out of the template source into a Jinja2 context variable ({{ term }}), restoring the code/data boundary; Flask does autoescape render_template_string when filename is None, so the claim holds, and output is unchanged for benign search terms.
